name: International Paper
description: International Paper makes corrugated boxes and the containerboard (linerboard and fluting) they are made from, sold mainly to industrial goods, food and beverage, e-commerce and agricultural customers. It runs paper mills that turn wood and recycled fiber into containerboard, then converts most of that into boxes and other packaging in its own plants. Since buying DS Smith (a European packaging group) for $9.9 billion on January 31, 2025, roughly a third of sales are in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Money comes from selling boxes and paper by the ton or box at prices that move with the packaging cycle, against fixed mill costs, so volume, price, mill downtime and energy and fiber costs drive profit. In 2026 it is preparing to split into two listed companies (North America and EMEA) and has sold its pulp business.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Materials' and Sub-Industry 'Paper & Plastic Packaging Products & Materials' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry, so industry group and industry are null (not sourced). SEC SIC code 2621 (Paper Mills) per EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: 6400 Poplar Avenue, Memphis, TN 38197 (EDGAR business address); New York corporation incorporated 1941 as successor to a 1898 company (FY2025 10-K Item 1)

employees.note: About 62,602 employees, about 30,421 in the US; 11,498 US employees are union-represented (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Packaging Solutions North America (PS NA)
businessLines.how: Customers (box buyers in food, agriculture, e-commerce and industrial goods, and box converters) pay per ton of containerboard or per box shipped, mostly on repeat orders; profit is the spread between sales price and mill, fiber, energy, freight and conversion costs, so price, volume and mill outage costs drive it.
businessLines.description: Containerboard mills and box (corrugated) plants in the US, Canada and Latin America, including the DS Smith North American assets (2025 PS NA included DS Smith sales of $611M).

revenue.note: FY2024: $14,293M. Source: FY2025 10-K segment note and MD&A

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024: $14,293M. Source: FY2025 10-K segment note and MD&A

operatingProfit.note: Business segment operating profit (before interest, corporate expenses, special items and non-operating pension); FY2024: $891M. Includes DS Smith business at a loss of $346M; 2025 also includes $564M higher depreciation from accelerated depreciation on mill strategic actions

businessLines.name: Packaging Solutions EMEA (PS EMEA)
businessLines.how: Same model as North America: European customers pay per box or per ton of recycled containerboard; margin depends on price, recycled-fiber and energy costs (energy subsidies timing is called out in the 10-K outlook), and volumes in a soft demand environment.
businessLines.description: Europe, Middle East and Africa packaging, formed mostly from the DS Smith acquisition (2025 PS EMEA included DS Smith sales of $7.2B); legacy IP EMEA sales were lower in 2025.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating loss; FY2024 profit $60M; DS Smith business lost $321M in the segment

brands.name: DS Smith (acquired Jan 31, 2025 for $9.9B)
brands.share: About 33% of FY2025 net sales ($7.2B in PS EMEA plus $611M in PS NA of $23,634M), computed from the 10-K; only 11 months of ownership

brands.name: Global Cellulose Fibers (pulp)
brands.note: Sold to American Industrial Partners for $1.5B, completed January 23, 2026, including $190M of preferred stock issued to IP (10-K; Q2 2026 10-Q)

brands.name: NORPAC (North Pacific Paper Company, Longview, Washington)
brands.note: Acquired June 4, 2026 for $368M subject to post-closing adjustments (Q2 2026 10-Q)

whatsNext.text: Separation into two independent listed companies (Packaging Solutions North America and Packaging Solutions EMEA), announced Jan 29, 2026; aimed for the end of 2026 or early 2027
Two greenfield packaging plants announced in 2025
